concepts.title: Ocean Currents and Their Effects
concepts.definition: Ocean currents are continuous flows of surface water set up by prevailing winds, coriolis force, density differences and coastline shapes, with warm currents flowing from equator to poles and cold currents from poles to equator, meeting at convergence zones rich in fisheries like the Grand Banks.
concepts.key_idea: Warm currents like the Gulf Stream warm western Europe, cold currents like the Labrador cause fog off Newfoundland, and their meeting grounds give the world's best fishing grounds.

concepts.title: Waves and Tides of the Ocean
concepts.definition: Waves are oscillatory movements raised by wind friction travelling through the water, while tides are rhythmic rises and falls caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun, giving spring tides at new and full moon and neap tides at quarter phases.
concepts.key_idea: Tides serve navigation, fishing and tidal power generation, and their twice-daily rhythm depends on the relative positions of earth, moon and sun.

concepts.title: Importance of Ocean Movements for Navigation, Climate and Economy
concepts.definition: Ocean currents, waves and tides aid and hinder navigation, moderate coastal climates, concentrate fisheries, generate tidal power and shape coasts, so the movements of ocean water carry both economic value and hazards that mariners and planners must respect.
concepts.key_idea: Ships use favourable currents to save fuel, while storms at sea generate the largest waves that threaten navigation.
